title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
slides: Cerebras CEO calls AI doomsday warnings a dangerous distraction?
The company builds the world's largest computer chip for AI.
Doomsday narratives often come from competitors with something to lose.
Ignore the hype and judge AI by real-world results.
Ask: who benefits from keeping you afraid?
thread_text:
1. The CEO Who Built the Biggest Chip

Cerebras Systems created the world's largest AI processor — a wafer-scale engine. Its CEO now says doomsday warnings are a dangerous distraction.

2. Doomsday Warnings Come From Competitors

When someone warns AI will kill us all, check who funds the warning. Often it's rivals who have a lot to lose if this technology wins.

3. Ignore the Hype, Judge Results

Real-world benchmarks and deployed systems matter more than apocalyptic predictions. Look at what AI actually does, not what it might do.

4. Ask Who Benefits From Fear

Fear sells headlines and stokes regulation. If your competitor is afraid, maybe your product works. Follow the incentives.

5. Test It Yourself

Pick one AI tool you already use. Run a real task and measure the outcome. Then tell me: did it save time or just add noise?
